title: Octavian, Caesar's Heir
objective: After this level you can explain how Caesar's young heir built power after the assassination.
summary: Caesar’s will made his 18-year-old great-nephew Octavian his heir. Octavian joined Antony and Lepidus, and they crushed the assassins at Philippi.

cards.headline: Caesar’s will named an heir almost no one expected: an 18-year-old.
cards.body: Caesar was dead, and his will handed a teenager his name. What can an 18-year-old do with a name? Quite a lot, it turned out.

cards.headline: The boy with the famous name
cards.body: Caesar’s will did more than leave his great-nephew a gift. It adopted Octavian, then 18, as his son and heir. Octavian took the name Gaius Julius Caesar, and he put it to work: it won over Caesar’s soldiers and supporters, who rallied to the man carrying it. Most heirs inherit the furniture. Octavian inherited Caesar’s fans, and a lot of them had swords.

cards.headline: Three men, again
cards.body: Remember the First Triumvirate, the informal deal between Caesar, Pompey and Crassus? In 43 BCE Octavian formed a second one with Mark Antony and Lepidus, and this time it was official: an alliance given legal power for five years. At Philippi in 42 BCE, Antony and Octavian defeated Caesar’s assassins, Brutus and Cassius, who both took their own lives. Two years after the Ides of March, the heir had outlasted the killers.
cards.callout: Unlike the First, the Second Triumvirate had legal power

cards.fact: Cicero was killed in the proscriptions of 43 BCE.
cards.context: The triumvirs brought back Sulla’s old idea: published lists of enemies who could be killed and their property seized. Cicero, Rome’s greatest orator, had attacked Antony in fierce speeches, and his name was on the list. Rome’s best talker had picked a fight with the wrong man.

cards.headline: The heir: rising
learned: Caesar adopted Octavian in his will
The Second Triumvirate formed in 43 BCE

questions.prompt: How was Octavian related to Julius Caesar?

options.label: Caesar’s great-nephew, adopted in his will
His younger brother, a fellow general

His rival general in Gaul
options.rationale: Octavian was a teenager when Caesar died.

It won over Caesar’s soldiers and supporters
